content.thinking: I should strip revision names like 5470c1a out of the root_cause field and rewrite it accordingly.

action_items.item: Add a CI test that runs the previous revision's summary cache reader against entries the new revision writes, and the reverse, for any change to a shared cache entry format.
Configure io-shop rollouts to halt and roll back automatically when the error rate rises above its baseline during the rollout.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop so that it pages the on-call engineer.
Find out why the rolling update of 696c33a stopped half-way and stayed paused.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests failed because reading the shopper's cached spend summary raised a ValueError: the cache entry '{G3714.1}' was not a figure in cents.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 5470c1a: the metrics read between it and the onset show the service at its usual error rate of {errors_before}, and account pages rendered normally until just before the onset.
A feature flag change: the flag provider's history shows no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before {T16.4}.
Shoppers closing the connection: those account page failures stopped before the onset.

causal_chain.step: Entries in that two-field form were in the cache because revision 696c33a, deployed at {P2.1}, changed a summary cache entry from a bare cents figure to text holding the figure and the purchase count, written as 'amount/items', under the same shopper.

A reader that expected a bare cents figure still read those entries because the rollout had stopped half-way. As of {T10.1}, {T10.2} of {T10.3} replicas ran 696c33a and {T10.5} still ran the old revision 5470c1a, with the rolling update paused and both revisions sharing the cache.
The old revision's reader raises an error on any entry that is not a bare cents figure, and that error fails the page.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A new version of the shop changed how it stores each shopper's saved spending summary, and while the update was stuck half-way, the older version still running beside it could not read the new kind of entry and failed the shopper's account page.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that tested whether the revision being replaced could read the new summary cache entry format before the change went out.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The mismatch between the new entry format and the old revision's reader would have been caught before deploy, and the change would have been held back or made readable by both revisions.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No rollout safeguard was seen that halts or rolls back a rollout when the service's error rate rises while revisions are mixed.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The rollout of the new revision would have been rolled back as soon as errors rose, without waiting for the alert and a manual rollback.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent found that the rollout of 696c33a was paused with the old and new revisions serving side by side.
Argus read the flag provider's history, which ruled out a flag change.
The Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop off revision 696c33a.
The Mitigation Agent checked the service and confirmed that the rollback had worked.
Code-Fix saw that its fix would not help on its own and kept none of it, so no partial fix was merged.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.

input.root_cause: The new revision changed what a summary cache entry holds, from a bare cents figure to one piece of text carrying the figure and the purchase count ('amount/items'), and wrote it where the previous revision, still serving alongside it, reads. The previous revision's reader raises a ValueError on any entry that is not a figure in cents, and that error failed the account page instead of the page working the figure out again.
input.still_at_risk: Deploying the new revision again while any replica still runs the old one could make account pages fail in the same way.
